Run the three “Next Commands” in the order shown. That will (1) search module-level candidates and select a best, (2) run system-level candidates, and (3) generate a targeted “next fix” report based on the current registry state.

### Recommended execution (in order)

```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --run --select-best
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml --run
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```

### What to look for after each step

1) **`aub_autopilot.py ... --select-best`**
- Expect: candidate runs + an update indicating a selected best module candidate (or none, if nothing beats the champion).
- Check: where it writes results (often under a `baseline/reports/` or a run directory). Confirm whether it updated any “current best” pointer or produced a diff/patch artifact.

2) **`system_autopilot.py ... --run`**
- Expect: system-level candidate evaluations (can be slower / more variable).
- Check: whether any system candidate beats the current champion on the same metrics (tuning/lockbox mean/min). If you see gains only in mean but regressions in min (or vice versa), note it—your selection criteria might be min-gated.

3) **`aub_next_fix.py ... --output ...`**
- Expect: a markdown report suggesting the next highest-leverage fix based on failures/regressions observed so far.
- Check: that `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` is generated and references the latest run artifacts (not stale paths).

### Common gotchas
- Make sure you’re on the intended branch/commit and that the `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` referenced in the handoff is present and unchanged.
- If results look “too good/bad,” confirm the run used the correct registry/spec files and the expected seeds/splits.
- If `--select-best` selects nothing, that’s still actionable: use `next_fix.md` to target the failure mode instead of adding more candidates.

If you paste the stdout/stderr (or the generated report paths) after running step 1, I can help interpret whether a new best was actually selected and what changed relative to the champion.
